learning_outcomes.text: Master fundamental concepts of technical thermodynamics, interpret thermal phenomena through this knowledge.
Know and use thermodynamic diagrams (p-v, T-s, h-s, Mollier) as tools for analyzing thermal phenomena.
Be able to represent processes in studied thermal machines and installations in diagrams and perform comparative analyses, highlighting advantages and disadvantages.

Know functional schemes of thermal machines and installations and be able to describe their operation based on these schemes and in correlation with thermodynamic cycle representation in p-v, T-s, h-s diagrams.
Know the main thermophysical properties of various thermodynamic agents and explain restrictions in using certain agents, such as freons.
Understand how thermal energy transfers in space and/or between physical systems and the main characteristics and mechanisms of conduction, convection, and thermal radiation.
Know specific physical quantities governing heat transfer phenomena.
Master mathematical models based on heat transfer laws and be able to solve simple transfer cases.
Know the role of heat exchangers in various thermal systems and equipment, main types of exchangers, flow schemes, exchanger equations, and elements of thermal design calculation.
Use digital tools for thermal calculation and experimental data processing.
Master experimental procedures for collecting measurement data on various thermal systems.
Operate laboratory equipment used for studying and analyzing thermal phenomena.
Critically evaluate thermal processes and be able to propose solutions to improve and mitigate identified disadvantages.
Be able to develop professional projects of medium complexity in the field of thermal engineering.
Select and analyze specific bibliographic sources in mechanical engineering.
Demonstrate autonomy in learning specific mechanical engineering issues.

Respect ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrate into the work group, apply relationship and efficient teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously inform and document themselves in their field of activity by adequately using effective lifelong learning methods and techniques.

syllabus_topics: Properties of pure substances. Vapors. Pure substance. Phase transformations, phase equilibrium. Vaporization at constant pressure. Thermodynamic parameters on limit curves; saturated and superheated vapors, vapor quality. Thermodynamic diagrams used for vapors. Calculation of state quantities for saturated liquid, saturated and superheated vapors, specific cases for water vapor. Vapor state transformations. Vapor throttling.
Cycles of vapor power plants. Carnot cycle. Rankine cycle with superheating. Ways to increase Rankine cycle efficiency. Cogeneration.
Cycles of vapor refrigeration plants. Generalities. Refrigerants. Vapor mechanical compression refrigeration plants. Absorption refrigeration plants.
Thermodynamics of humid air. Introduction. Characteristic state quantities. (h-x) diagram. Simple processes and representation in (h-x) diagram. Air conditioning and climatization schemes.

Thermal conduction. Introduction. Fundamental quantities. Fourier's law. Conductive heat transfer in steady thermal regime (homogeneous and non-homogeneous bodies - simple geometries, homogeneous bodies without internal heat sources - type I and III conditions).
Thermal convection. Newton's law. Basic elements and concepts. Influences on thermal convection. Basic differential equations. Similarity method. Free convection. Forced convection.
Thermal radiation. Mechanism of thermal radiation. Laws of thermal radiation. Radiative heat transfer between bodies separated by diathermal media. Radiation shields.
Heat exchangers. Classification, construction, operation. Flow schemes. Equations of heat exchangers. Temperature diagrams. Logarithmic mean temperature difference. Thermal design calculation.
Vapors
Vapor power cycles
Vapor refrigeration cycles
Humid air
Air conditioning plants
Thermal conduction
Thermal convection
Occupational safety. Experimental data processing. Errors.

Thermometry II
Determination of parameters of wet saturated steam
Determination of air humidity
Determination of the adiabatic exponent of air by Clement-Desormes method
Joule-Thomson effect
Thermodynamics test
Electro-analogic modeling for steady-state two-dimensional thermal fields
Determination of the heat transfer coefficient from a single smooth pipe to air in unperturbed free convection
Determination of the energetic emission factor of bodies (blackness degree)
Determination of the convective coefficient for heat transfer in a fluidized bed
Final test
Recovery session
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Integer grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the granting of corresponding study credits. All laboratory works must be completed; recovery is allowed for only one outstanding laboratory work.
